builder.objective: REPAIR V3-06: Move the cursor advance inside the same transaction as materialization (e.g. applyDeltas advances the pull cursor before committing, or pullDeltas passes the cursor update into the transactional callback). Extend the in-memory withTransaction to snapshot/restore ALL affected repos (expenses, settlements, tasks, members, memberships, households, and the sync buffer/cursor state). Add a test that injects a real failing materialization (a repo error, not a silently-skipped malformed payload) and asserts the cursor did not advance AND no business table was partially updated.; When the local record wins the conflict, preserve the local dirty record in the buffer (do not overwrite it with the remote record); only store the remote record when the remote wins. Add a test: local write -> pull of same id with lower remote revision -> assert business entity is LOCAL AND getDirtyRecords still returns the LOCAL payload which pushDeltas sends.; Wire the scoped facade (or equivalent membership check) into the data-access path actually used by the app: AppContext/use-cases must obtain repos scoped to the current user (caller userId) so every getByHousehold/create/update/delete verifies membership, and ledger mutations go through assertLedgerWrite-style validation. Hostile tests must exercise the path the app uses (e.g. through AppContext or the use-case layer), not only a manually constructed facade.; Add a test that runs the sync pipeline (applyDeltas materialization + wrapper dirty recording + pushDeltas) against the SQLite-backed repositories (using the mocked expo-sqlite driver already used in repositories.test.ts), or a shared contract test executed against both implementations, proving remote delta -> business record readable and local write -> getDirtyRecords payload.
builder.scope: Repair only the audited must-fix findings on the preserved V3 baseline; do not rebuild accepted work.
acceptance: applyDeltas materializes pulled records into business tables (contribution_entries, expense_entries, settlements, todo_items, persistent_tasks, members, memberships, households) inside a transaction
storeLocalRecords has callers and getDirtyRecords returns real payloads; pushDeltas sends actual local writes
group-options UI reachable from group settings: unit toggle (Minutes|Points) with provenance warning, compensation toggle + rate
invitation UI: invite action with share sheet, /join/:token deep-link route, atomic acceptance (membership + member)
authorization rules enforced in data-access path: tenant isolation on reads/writes, deterministic conflict resolution replacing blind LWW in applyDeltas
hostile tests: cross-tenant read blocked, balance falsification rejected, concurrent same-id edits resolved deterministically
end-to-end sync tests: remote delta materializes into business data, local write appears in getDirtyRecords and is pushed
